svg.title: At 1000 this patient had a Glasgow Coma Scale of 9, a sluggish right pupil, heart rate 52, blood pressure 178/70, and an intracranial pressure of 26 mm Hg. Mannitol was given. Highlight the findings in the 1100 note that show the therapy is working.
svg.desc: The Cushing response present at 1000, a rising blood pressure with a widened pulse pressure and bradycardia, has resolved, so the normal heart rate and pressure are outcome evidence rather than background data. A better level of consciousness, a briskly reactive pupil, and a pressure back near the normal range say the mannitol worked. Normal adult intracranial pressure is usually cited as roughly 5 to 15 mm Hg, sources differ slightly, and values above about 20 to 25 mm Hg prompt treatment. Head-of-bed elevation and a midline neck are interventions being maintained, not signs of improvement.
